chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Misma', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) judged regarding the tooth of a child before it extrudes, [paying] a camel for each tooth in each age.

key_terms.بَعِيراً بَعِيراً: a camel for each (one by one)

ai.seo_question: What is the blood money for a child's tooth before it erupts according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi details Imam Ali’s (peace be upon him) judicial ruling on the gradual payment of blood money (diyah) for a child’s teeth before they fully erupt, establishing a precedent for proportional compensation in personal injury law. It highlights the precision of early Shia jurisprudence in handling developmental stages of the body, linking physical growth to legal liability. The ruling underscores the principle that compensation scales with the degree of maturity or completeness of the affected body part.
